Current vLLM consequently feeds projected image features into Gemma at `1 / sqrt(hidden_size)` of their intended magnitude. Before #36787, the operations were balanced: ```text text: embed_tokens ------------------------> Gemma.forward * sqrt(H) image: projector / sqrt(H) -> merge --------> Gemma.forward * sqrt(H) ``` After #36787, current vLLM scales only text: ```text text: embed_tokens * sqrt(H) -> merge -> Gemma.forward unchanged image: projector / sqrt(H) ----> merge -> Gemma.forward unchanged ``` Current `main` scales text in [`gemma.py:284-308`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/60c3a31b12b0a735baa79684885391747771ec64/vllm/model_executor/models/gemma.py#L284-L308), but still inverse-scales images in [`paligemma.py:376-383`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/60c3a31b12b0a735baa79684885391747771ec64/vllm/model_executor/models/paligemma.py#L376-L383). Multimodal merge only replaces placeholder rows, and `GemmaModel.forward(inputs_embeds=...)` applies no compensating scale. Transformers changed both halves atomically in [`0e7cb4e3`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/commit/0e7cb4e3ea3daaeef626148522f80b751e9559bd): Gemma text lookup gained `sqrt(H)` scaling and PaliGemma stopped dividing projected image features. Transformers 5.14.1 directly inserts raw projected image features into the already-scaled text embeddings. For ColPali's `hidden_size=2048`, the contract reduction is: ```python import math hidden_size = 2048 raw_projected_image = 1.0 print( "before #36787:", raw_projected_image * hidden_size**-0.5 * math.sqrt(hidden_size), ) print("current vLLM:", raw_projected_image * hidden_size**-0.5) print("expected:", raw_projected_image) ``` ```text before #36787: 1.0 current vLLM: 0.022097086912079608 expected: 1.0 ``` The stale factor is therefore about `0.0221`: projected image features enter Gemma at about 2.21% of their intended magnitude. Controlled one-variable A/B against the pinned Transformers reference: | Variant | Text cosine mean | Image cosine mean | Image p01 | Image minimum | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Current stale inverse scale | 0.999797 | 0.903149 | 0.430221 | 0.225688 | | Inverse scale removed only | 0.999797 | 0.987502 | 0.726556 | 0.436249 | The request, preprocessing, checkpoint, plugin SHA, and reference were held constant; only `vision_embeddings *= hidden_size**-0.5` was removed. The remaining image mismatch is a separately measured Neuron eager-vision drift, so this one-line change should not be represented as fixing all ColPali parity issues. Full ColPali command used for validation: ```bash vllm serve vidore/colpali-v1.3-hf \ --revision 7d3c8ab1c1908b32d701308fb1dfb2968d150c67 \ --served-model-name vidore/colpali-v1.3-hf \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --max-num-seqs 1 \ --max-model-len 4096 \ --trust-remote-code \ --runner pooling \ --convert none \ --pooler-config.task token_embed \ --port 20000 ``` Expected behavior: PaliGemma should return raw projected image features from `embed_multimodal()`, matching Transformers' scaled-text/raw-image contract. Suggested fix: ```diff def embed_multimodal(self, **kwargs: object) -> MultiModalEmbeddings: image_input = self._parse_and_validate_image_input(**kwargs) if image_input is None: return [] vision_embeddings = self._process_image_input(image_input) - vision_embeddings = vision_embeddings * (self.config.hidden_size**-0.5) return vision_embeddings ``` Suggested tests: pass known projected `image_embeds` to PaliGemma and assert they are returned unchanged; add one fixed-image Transformers parity test that compares first-step logits or top-k probabilities. Current ColPali tests verify shape, L2 normalization, and weak relevance ordering, which cannot detect this pre-language-model scaling error. The final downstream ColPali branch passes with pristine vLLM only because its host-vision path supplies raw projected features and bypasses `PaliGemma.embed_multimodal()`. The one-line patch is not part of that final plugin apply set, and the pristine pass does not validate the stale upstream method. This regression was introduced by #36787 (`65986db6ba71abf4cf0639c5fd1477b0d8df8f5e`). Searches for PaliGemma image scaling, inverse scaling, `sqrt(hidden_size)`, `hidden_size**-0.5`, and #36787 found no matching issue or follow-up fix. Severity: major silent correctness regression. The source contract is confirmed; broad current-main CUDA generation impact has not yet been quantified. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: FP8 on RDNA3/gfx1100 exceeds the 600 s engine-ready timeout on first start — no AMD_Radeon_Graphics tuned configs shipped
items.body:
### TL;DR - The official FP8 checkpoint (Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8) **loads and serves fine on a consumer RDNA3 card** (gfx1100, Radeon W7900 48 GB, `vllm==0.27.1+rocm723` on ROCm). There is no architecture refusal — community trackers currently report FP8 as "does not run on RDNA3", but it does. - The out-of-the-box failure is a **startup timeout**: for `device_name=AMD_Radeon_Graphics` the wheel ships **zero** tuned W8A8 block-FP8 configs (of 218 device-keyed configs it ships 76 for AMD Instinct and 142 for NVIDIA devices), so the default config is used and warmup **JIT-compiles the Triton GEMM kernels shape by shape**. First engine init measured **1474.26 s** — 2.5x the 600 s default of `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` — and the APIServer aborts. - The abort message says the timeout is "**often caused by slow weight loading**". Our weights loaded in **16.33 s**; the 23+ minutes between kernel warnings were CPU-side Triton compilation with the GPU idle. - `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=1800` makes it start. Once the on-disk Triton cache is warm, engine init is **49 s** and every later start is ~2 min — the cost is one-time per host (until `~/.triton/cache` is cleared). - **Asks:** (1) ship tuned W8A8 configs for `AMD_Radeon_Graphics` (mirroring the MI300X/MI325 sets); (2) cheap: mention cold-start JIT/config warmup as a cause in the engine-ready timeout error or the env-var docs; (3) secondary observation: the **first inference** triggers a further ~43 min of JIT staging that `/health` does not reflect. - **I have the hardware** and am happy to run whatever tuning/profiling procedure you point at and PR the resulting `AMD_Radeon_Graphics` JSONs, and to test any RC on gfx1100. ### Your current environment
Output of python -m vllm.collect_env (venv used for all runs below) ```text Collecting environment information... uv is set ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Clang version : Could not collect CMake version : version 3.28.3 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.11.0+gitd0c8b1f Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : N/A ROCM used to build PyTorch : 7.2.53211 XPU used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.3 (main, Mar 3 2026, 12:15:18) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-6.8.0-79-generic-x86_64-with-glibc-2.39 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : Could not collect CUDA_MODULE_LOADING set to : GPU models and configuration : AMD Radeon Graphics (gfx1100) Nvidia driver version : Could not collect cuDNN version : Could not collect HIP runtime version : 7.2.53211 MIOpen runtime version : 3.5.1 Is XNNPACK available : True ============================== vLLM Info ============================== ROCM Version : 7.2.53211-e1a6bc5663 vLLM Version : 0.27.1 vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled GPU Topology: single GPU, NUMA node 0 ============================== Environment Variables ============================== PYTORCH_NVML_BASED_CUDA_CHECK=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_root ``` Install (per the ROCm install docs): `uv pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/` → `vllm==0.27.1+rocm723`; `transformers==5.15.0`; host ROCm userspace 7.2.1. CPU: 2x AMD EPYC 9334 (full `lscpu` flags and the rocm-smi topology table omitted for brevity; available on request).
### 🐛 Describe the bug **Expected:** `vllm serve` (or `api_server`) with an official FP8 checkpoint on gfx1100 either starts within the default engine-ready budget, or fails with a message pointing at the real cost. **Actual (measured on Radeon W7900D, gfx1100, 48 GB):** | Run | `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` | Triton cache | Result | |---|---|---|---| | cold serve | 600 (default) | cold | `TimeoutError` at 600 s mid-warmup; weights had loaded in 16.33 s | | cold serve | 1800 | cold | engine init **1474.26 s**, then `/health` 200, serving OK | | warm re-run | 1800 | warm | engine init **49.01 s** | | later starts (x3) | 1800 | warm | 49.10 / 49.11 / 49.19 s, server up in ~2 min | After unlock, serving works end-to-end (105/105 benchmark requests OK) — at untuned-config performance; see measured results below. #### Reproduce without hardware (2 minutes) Anyone with the wheel installed can verify the config gap that drives the cold-start cost: ```bash CFG=$(python -c "import vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.fp8_utils as m, os; print(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(m.__file__),'configs'))") ls "$CFG" | wc -l # 219 (218 device-keyed JSONs + README.md) ls "$CFG" | grep -c MI300X # 28 (+ 24 MI325X + 24 MI325_OAM = 76 Instinct) ls "$CFG" | grep -ci radeon # 0 ls "$CFG" | grep -c 'N=16384,K=5120' # 0 — not shipped for ANY device ``` The engine-side lookup is a plain file-exists check in `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py` (0.27.1, ~line 830): the filename is built from `get_device_name_as_file_name()` — which on RDNA3 consumer cards is literally the torch device name `AMD Radeon Graphics` → `device_name=AMD_Radeon_Graphics` — and when the JSON is missing the code logs the warning below and **returns `None` (default config)**. Nothing is ever written back to that directory, so the cost recurs for every fresh host/venv. #### Reproduce on gfx1100 (~35 min, needs a 24 GB+ RDNA3 card) ```bash # fresh venv — a warm ~/.triton/cache hides the bug (init drops to ~49 s) uv venv /root/venv-fp8 && VIRTUAL_ENV=/root/venv-fp8 uv pip install vllm \ --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/ # 0.27.1+rocm723 # model: official FP8 checkpoint, ~28.7 GiB # HF: huggingface-cli download Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 # (we used ModelScope: modelscope download Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8) SNAP=/path/to/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 # 1) default timeout → aborts at 600 s: /root/venv-fp8/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model "$SNAP" --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \ --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --port 8199 # 2) unlocked: VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=1800 /root/venv-fp8/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model "$SNAP" --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \ --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --port 8199 ``` (All measurements above were taken with `--enforce-eager` added to skip torch.compile/CUDA-graph capture; the cold abort also reproduces without it, with `torch.compile took 67.53 s` interleaved.) #### Verbatim evidence
1) Cold run, default timeout — aborts while weights were long done ```text (EngineCore pid=280186) INFO 08-17 01:42:46 [default_loader.py:430] Loading weights took 16.33 seconds (EngineCore pid=280186) INFO 08-17 01:42:46 [gpu_model_runner.py:5405] Model loading took 29.38 GiB memory and 17.353099 seconds (EngineCore pid=280186) INFO 08-17 01:44:23 [monitor.py:53] torch.compile took 67.53 s in total (EngineCore pid=280186) WARNING 08-17 01:44:23 [fp8_utils.py:851] Using default W8A8 Block FP8 kernel config. Performance might be sub-optimal! Config file not found at /root/venv-fp8probe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/configs/N=16384,K=5120,device_name=AMD_Radeon_Graphics,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128,128].json (EngineCore pid=280186) WARNING 08-17 02:07:49 [fp8_utils.py:851] Using default W8A8 Block FP8 kernel config. Performance might be sub-optimal! Config file not found at /root/venv-fp8probe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/configs/N=5120,K=6144,device_name=AMD_Radeon_Graphics,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128,128].json (APIServer pid=279547) TimeoutError: Timed out waiting for engine core processes to start. This is often caused by slow weight loading for large models. Waited 600s (configured by VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S). To increase the timeout, set the environment variable: VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S= ``` Note the **23 m 26 s gap between the two fp8_utils warnings** — that is one Triton GEMM kernel compiling (single CPU core pinned, GPU idle), not weight loading.
2) Same wheel, timeout raised — starts, and the cost is visible ```text (EngineCore pid=371418) WARNING 08-17 08:07:37 [fp8_utils.py:851] Using default W8A8 Block FP8 kernel config. ... N=16384,K=5120,device_name=AMD_Radeon_Graphics,... (EngineCore pid=371418) WARNING 08-17 08:31:17 [fp8_utils.py:851] Using default W8A8 Block FP8 kernel config. ... N=34816,K=5120,device_name=AMD_Radeon_Graphics,... (EngineCore pid=371418) INFO 08-17 08:31:42 [core.py:355] init engine (profile, create kv cache, warmup model) took 1474.26 s (APIServer pid=371094) INFO: 127.0.0.1:33878 - "GET /health HTTP/1.1" 200 OK ``` The warmup pass walks five GEMM shapes for this model (N=16384/K=5120, N=5120/K=6144, N=34816/K=5120, N=5120/K=17408, N=14336/K=5120); none has a shipped config.
3) Warm Triton cache — the whole cliff disappears ```text (EngineCore pid=378832) INFO 08-17 08:38:28 [core.py:355] init engine (profile, create kv cache, warmup model) took 49.01 s (APIServer pid=378511) INFO 08-17 08:38:45 [api_server.py:682] Starting vLLM server on http://0.0.0.0:8199 (APIServer pid=378511) INFO: Application startup complete. (APIServer pid=378511) INFO: 127.0.0.1:46230 - "GET /health HTTP/1.1" 200 OK ```
4) Secondary: first-INFERENCE JIT staging (~43 min), invisible to /health Even after a healthy start, the first completion request triggers more JIT compiles; the server answers `/health` 200 the whole time and a default-timeout client (ours: 300 s) just times out. Verbatim from the first served request on a cache-warm-start server: ```text (EngineCore pid=434612) WARNING 08-17 13:34:18 [chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py:419] Cannot use ROCm custom paged attention kernel, falling back to Triton implementation. (EngineCore pid=434612) WARNING 08-17 13:55:59 [jit_monitor.py:135] Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: _causal_conv1d_update_kernel. This causes a latency spike; consider extending warmup to cover this shape/config. (EngineCore pid=434612) WARNING 08-17 13:55:59 [jit_monitor.py:135] Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode_kernel. ... (EngineCore pid=434612) WARNING 08-17 13:55:59 [jit_monitor.py:135] Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: layer_norm_fwd_kernel. ... ``` The very first request (13:34:18) outlived the client's 300 s ceiling; the first fully-served response landed at ~14:17:41 — **43 min after the first request was sent** (the request that completed was issued 14:07:52 and took `total_s=608.536757`). Subsequent traffic is normal: a 16-request warmup burst after this returned all 200 in ~26–28 s.
### Root cause (as far as the code shows) 1. `fp8_utils.py` builds the tuned-config filename from the torch device name — on RDNA3 consumer cards that is `AMD Radeon Graphics` → `device_name=AMD_Radeon_Graphics` — and the wheel ships **no** JSONs for that name (the entire AMD set is Instinct-only). Missing file → warning → `return None` → default W8A8 config. 2. With the default config, `w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm` JIT-compiles its Triton kernel for each distinct (N, K) shape during engine warmup. On this host each big compile takes ~20+ min of single-threaded CPU (GPU idle); the shape-by-shape walk (first warning 08:07:37 → init done 08:31:42) accounts for essentially all of the 1474.26 s engine init. 3. The APIServer's engine-ready deadline (default 600 s, `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S`, consumed in the v1 engine core client) expires mid-warmup, and the error names "slow weight loading" as the likely cause. 4. The Triton disk cache (`~/.triton/cache`) makes every subsequent start fast, and nothing writes tuned JSONs back — so the cliff is a **per-host one-time cost that looks like a hard failure** the first time. ### Proposed fixes (ranked) 1. **Ship tuned W8A8 block-FP8 configs for `AMD_Radeon_Graphics`** (gfx1100 at minimum), mirroring the shipped MI300X/MI325 sets. This is what the runtime warning already asks for, it removes the "sub-optimal default" path entirely, and it is the lever for the performance gap below. I have a W7900 and am glad to run the config-generation/benchmark procedure on it and open a PR with the resulting JSONs if you can point me at the tooling. 2. **Cheap message/docs improvement:** `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` is documented, but the timeout error's cause list ("often caused by slow weight loading") sends users down the wrong path when the real cost is JIT/config warmup on an untuned device (weights: 16.33 s here). One extra sentence in the error string or in the env-var docs — "first-start JIT compilation of untuned kernels can take tens of minutes on newly-supported platforms; raise the timeout or pre-warm" — would have saved us hours. 3. **Secondary observation** (same platform gap, different surface): the first inference after a cold start triggers ~43 min more of Triton JIT that `/health` does not reflect (details block 4). If preferred I'll split this into its own issue — keeping it here because it shares the root cause (no RDNA3 tuning artifacts shipped). ### Measured results after unlock (context for prioritization, not a complaint) `--enforce-eager`, temp 0, fixed 100-token prompt, 128-token generations, 5 reps per cell, non-streaming: | concurrency | aggregate decode tok/s | requests OK | p50 request wall | |---|---:|---|---:| | 1 | 0.612 | 5/5 | 209.2 s | | 4 | 2.301 | 20/20 | 222.4 s | | 16 | 8.730 | 80/80 | 234.5 s | For scale on the same GPU, llama.cpp with a Q4_K_M GGUF of the same model does 28.6 tok/s single-stream and 164.4 tok/s aggregate at c=32 — so FP8-on-RDNA3 today is ~47x slower per stream, which the tuned-config gap plausibly explains a large part of. Capacity is not the issue: 29.38 GiB of FP8 weights on the 48 GB card with ~19 GiB headroom. ### Related issues (searched; not duplicates) - #51136 — AITER not enabled on RDNA3 (gfx1100): same GPU class, different mechanism (INT8/Quark + AITER gating vs FP8 W8A8 Triton path here); complementary data point. - #35547, #32116 — same engine-ready timeout symptom class on NVIDIA (slow weight loading / DeepGEMM warmup). This issue adds the RDNA3/FP8 instance where the dominant cost is per-shape Triton JIT under a missing tuned config, plus the configs gap itself. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] I searched existing issues (linked above) and found no report of FP8-on-RDNA3 failing startup via untuned-config JIT with this mechanism. - [x] `collect_env` output attached. - [x] Repro is self-contained; the configs-gap part needs no hardware. Happy to contribute: tuning runs on gfx1100 → `AMD_Radeon_Graphics` config PR, and RC testing on this card.

items.title: [Feature]: Optional content fallback policy for length-truncated reasoning responses
items.body:
#### Summary

When a DeepSeek V4 generation reaches `max_tokens` before its reasoning block closes, the Chat Completions response has `finish_reason: "length"`, `message.content: null`, and non-empty `message.reasoning`.

vLLM preserves the generated text, so this is not token loss. However, OpenAI-compatible clients that read only `content` present an empty assistant response.

Could vLLM provide a documented, explicit opt-in policy for deployments that prefer non-empty standard content on this path?

The default behavior can remain unchanged. An opt-in is important because copying incomplete reasoning into content can expose chain-of-thought text and can misrepresent an unfinished analysis as a final answer.

#### Relationship to existing work

- #48645 covers naturally completed replies that omit `</think>` and are misclassified as reasoning.
- #50753 proposes `force_nonempty_content` for that natural-stop case and deliberately excludes streaming responses with `finish_reason: "length"`.
- This request concerns whether deployments should have a separate explicit compatibility policy for the length-truncated case.

#### Environment

- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813`
- vLLM release: `0.27.1`
- vLLM nightly: `0.27.2rc1.dev122+g8efa13b70`, commit `8efa13b700f1836657699cae2503dc2feab27fa0`
- Hardware: Linux arm64, 4 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs
- Endpoint: `/v1/chat/completions`
- Parser: `deepseek_v4`
- Direct `vllm serve`, with no proxy or separate response assembler

Material server arguments:

```bash
vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 256 \
  --max-num-seqs 36 \
  --trust-remote-code
```

#### Reproduction

```bash
curl -sS http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813",
    "messages": [
      {
        "role": "user",
        "content": "Rank these by acidity and justify each comparison from first principles, considering inductive effects, resonance stabilisation, and hybridisation: phenol, ethanol, acetic acid, water, trifluoroacetic acid. Think step by step, then finish with \"the answer is (X)\"."
      }
    ],
    "max_tokens": 256,
    "temperature": 0,
    "chat_template_kwargs": {
      "enable_thinking": true
    }
  }' \
  | jq '.choices[0] | {finish_reason,content:.message.content,reasoning:.message.reasoning}'
```

Observed response shape:

```json
{
  "finish_reason": "length",
  "content": null,
  "reasoning": "<non-empty generated text>"
}
```

#### Results

For vLLM 0.27.1, all 48 requests capped at 256 through 2,048 tokens ended inside reasoning, returned null content, and returned non-empty reasoning.

For nightly `8efa13b70`, all 60 requests capped at 256 through 4,096 tokens had the same result.

At 4,096 tokens on vLLM 0.27.1, every response crossed the reasoning boundary and produced non-empty content. Ten later ended by length and two stopped normally. This shows that the condition is truncation inside reasoning, not any response with `finish_reason: "length"`.

Streaming reproduced the split in both builds. At 256 tokens, 12 of 12 streams per build emitted non-empty reasoning deltas and no non-empty content delta.

With thinking disabled on nightly, 12 of 12 requests at 256 tokens returned non-empty content and empty reasoning.

#### Requested behavior

Please consider one of these outcomes:

1. Document that length-truncated reasoning is available only in `reasoning`, and document that content-only clients must handle this response shape.
2. Add an explicit opt-in compatibility policy that copies or moves length-truncated reasoning into `content`.
3. Expose a terminal indicator that lets clients distinguish an empty answer from a response whose entire generation remains in the reasoning channel.

The option must behave consistently for streaming and non-streaming responses. It must not silently expose incomplete reasoning by default.

#### Duplicate check

I searched the current issue tracker. #48645 and #50753 are related but focus on naturally completed replies that omit the reasoning close marker. This request is limited to an explicit compatibility policy for responses that end by length while still reasoning.

items.title: [Bug]: Kimi-K3 silent output corruption in 1P1D NIXL Direct-PD disaggregated deployment
items.body: ### Summary I am seeing intermittent silent output corruption / garbled generation when serving Kimi-K3 with TP=8 in a 1P1D disaggregated Prefill/Decode deployment using MooncakeStoreConnector together with NixlConnector through MultiConnector. The important A/B observation is: - **NIXL-only PD**: stable, no garbled output observed. - **NIXL + MooncakeStoreConnector through MultiConnector**: garbled output reproducibly appears under sustained load. - **Mooncake enabled + DSpark/speculative decoding disabled**: corruption still reproduces. - **Mooncake disabled**: corruption has not reproduced in my testing. Therefore speculative decoding does not appear to be required to trigger the corruption. The corrupted requests can generate long sequences of nonsensical mixed-language/repeated tokens, for example repeated words such as `Effective/effective` mixed with unrelated English/Chinese fragments. Some affected streams eventually surface at the application layer as HTTP 502 / `7104_UPSTREAM_STREAM_INTERRUPTED`. This looks like a correctness issue rather than a crash-only issue: the engine can continue running while individual outputs are already corrupted. ### Deployment topology Two-node 1P1D deployment: ``` Prefill node Kimi-K3 TP=8 | | NIXL PD transfer v Decode node Kimi-K3 TP=8 ``` Failing configuration additionally uses: ``` Prefill | +-- MultiConnector | +-- NixlConnector | kv_role=kv_producer | +-- MooncakeStoreConnector kv_role=kv_both load_async=true lookup_async=true ``` The Decode node remains a NixlConnector consumer. ### Environment - **Model**: Kimi-K3 - **Tensor parallel size**: 8 - **PD topology**: 1 Prefill + 1 Decode - **KV transfer**: NIXL - **Prefix caching**: enabled - **KV cache dtype**: fp8 - **MLA prefill backend**: FLASHINFER - **VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT**: DS - **vLLM version**: Latest main / nightly - **vLLM commit**: Latest main - **GPU**: 8x NVIDIA B300 - **CUDA**: CUDA 12.8 - **OS / container image**: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 / Container) Relevant upstream fixes included: - #48425: yes (tested on latest main) - #49499: yes (tested on latest main) - #49502: yes (tested on latest main) - #50344: yes (tested on latest main) ### Failing Prefill configuration Relevant environment: ```bash export VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS export VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL=4608 ``` KV connector: ```json KV='{ "kv_connector": "MultiConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both", "kv_load_failure_policy": "fail", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "connectors": [ { "kv_connector": "NixlConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_load_failure_policy": "fail" }, { "kv_connector": "MooncakeStoreConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "load_async": true, "lookup_async": true } } ] } }' ``` Relevant server arguments: ```bash vllm serve /modules/Kimi-K3 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-config \ '{"mla_prefill_backend":"FLASHINFER","use_prefill_query_quantization":true}' \ --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --enforce-eager \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \ --kv-transfer-config "$KV" ``` *(For minimal reproduction, run without `--speculative-config`, as the corruption reproduces without DSpark).* ### Decode configuration The Decode side uses NIXL only: ```bash vllm serve /modules/Kimi-K3 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-config \ '{"mla_prefill_backend":"FLASHINFER","use_prefill_query_quantization":true}' \ --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --kv-transfer-config \ '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"}' \ --compilation-config \ '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \ --max-num-seqs 32 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 ``` ### Stable control configuration If I remove `MooncakeStoreConnector` / `MultiConnector` and use only: ```json --kv-transfer-config \ '{ "kv_connector": "NixlConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_load_failure_policy": "fail" }' ``` on the Prefill side, the same Kimi-K3 TP8 PD setup is stable in my testing. The control setup still uses: - Kimi-K3 - TP=8 - prefix caching enabled - FP8 KV cache - FLASHINFER MLA prefill - NIXL PD transfer I have also tested DSpark/speculative decoding in the NIXL-only configuration without observing the same corruption. ### Reproduction A minimal A/B reproduction: 1. **Test A — Control**: - Start Kimi-K3 TP8 Prefill with NixlConnector only. - Start Kimi-K3 TP8 Decode with NixlConnector. - Enable prefix caching. - Run sustained concurrent traffic, including repeated/shared prefixes. - Confirm prefix-cache activity. - **Result**: No corrupted output observed. 2. **Test B — Failing**: - Keep the same model and PD topology, but replace the Prefill connector with `MultiConnector` (`NixlConnector` + `MooncakeStoreConnector`). - Run the same traffic and make sure Mooncake external cache hits are occurring. - **Result**: Intermittent silent output corruption / garbled text. 3. **Test C — DSpark disabled**: - Repeat Test B without any `--speculative-config`. - **Result**: Corruption still reproduces. (Speculative decoding is not the primary trigger). ### Actual behavior Affected generations suddenly degrade into nonsensical output containing repeated and unrelated multilingual tokens. Example pattern: ``` ... effective ... Effective ... effective ... ... random unrelated English words ... ... Chinese fragments ... ... repeated/degenerate text ... ``` The server does not necessarily crash immediately. At the upper service layer, affected streams can end as: ``` HTTP 502 7104_UPSTREAM_STREAM_INTERRUPTED ``` ### Attachments I can provide: - screenshot of a corrupted generation; - Prometheus graphs from the failing run; - Prometheus graphs from the stable/control run; - complete Prefill/Decode logs around an affected request; - Mooncake hit/load metrics; - exact request ID / prompt and response if needed. ### Additional observation about speculative decoding When DSpark is enabled, I have also observed abnormal MTP/spec-decode acceptance behavior during some bad runs. However, I currently consider this a secondary symptom, because the output corruption can still reproduce after DSpark is completely disabled. Therefore this report is specifically about the Mooncake/external hybrid-cache path, rather than the DSpark rejection sampler. ### Expected behavior Loading a prefix from MooncakeStore should be correctness-equivalent to either: 1. recomputing the prefix, or 2. serving the same prefix from local GPU prefix cache. For Kimi-K3, all cache/state groups required to resume generation should represent the same safe token boundary. Enabling Mooncake external caching should not change model output correctness. ### Suspected area The A/B result suggests the issue is somewhere in the interaction between: - Kimi-K3 hybrid cache - `MooncakeStoreConnector` + `MultiConnector` - external prefix cache lookup/load - KDA recurrent state / attention KV reconciliation A possible failure mode would be a resume boundary where the attention KV and KDA recurrent state do not correspond to the same token position. I am particularly interested in whether the following invariant is always guaranteed for Mooncake external hits: ``` reported reusable prefix <= safe Full-Attention/MLA prefix <= valid boundary with corresponding KDA recurrent state ``` and whether all hybrid cache groups are invalidated/reconciled together if one external group is unavailable or has a shorter valid hit. ### Possibly related issues / PRs - #48425 — per-group prefix-hit divergence for hybrid models with KV connector - #49499 — Mooncake TP-sharded Mamba/linear-attention state corruption - #49502 — reliable partial-tail KV offload for sub-block prompts - #50344 — divergent hybrid cache hits scoped to capable connectors / MultiConnector behavior - #47812 — group-aware recovery for KV load failures on hybrid models - #50630 — hybrid recurrent-cache correctness / hit-boundary coordination discussion If my commit already contains them, this may indicate a remaining Kimi-K3-specific or MooncakeStore/MultiConnector-specific correctness path.

Observed response: ```text HTTP 200 ``` The returned content is valid and satisfies the schema: ```json { "status": "ok", "items": [1, 2, 3], "request_id": 0 } ``` This confirms that: - The model is loaded correctly. - The request format is valid. - The schema is accepted. - xgrammar can compile and enforce the schema. - `ngram_gpu` can complete at least one structured request. ## Concurrent-load result The script sends: ```text Request count: 24 Concurrency: 8 ``` Observed result with vLLM 0.27.1: ```text Successful valid JSON responses: 3 HTTP 500 responses: 21 Invalid HTTP 200 responses: 0 Transport errors: 0 Timeouts: 0 ``` The failed requests return: ```json { "error": { "code": 500, "message": "Internal server error", "param": null, "type": "InternalServerError" } } ``` ## Server log errors Representative server log output: ```text ERROR [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request ... for tokens 151667. Please file an issue. ``` ```text ERROR [scheduler.py:1835] Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [151667] for request ... Terminating request. ``` Other rejected token IDs observed in the same run include: ```text 22335 630 ``` The API server subsequently reports: ```text Request ... failed with an internal error during generation ``` The following log markers were all present: ```json { "failed_to_advance_fsm": true, "please_file_issue": true, "grammar_rejected_tokens": true, "internal_generation_error": true } ``` ## Server health after the failures After the 21 HTTP 500 responses, the script calls: ```text GET /v1/models ``` Observed result: ```text HTTP 200 ``` Therefore, this is a per-request internal generation failure rather than a complete server crash. ## Control without speculative decoding The script stops the failing server and starts an otherwise identical server without: ```text --speculative-config ``` The following settings remain unchanged: ```text Model Model dtype xgrammar backend JSON schema Prompts Request count Concurrency Maximum model length Maximum sequences Maximum batched tokens GPU ``` Control result: ```text Single request: HTTP 200, valid JSON Concurrent successful responses: 24 Concurrent HTTP 500 responses: 0 Invalid JSON responses: 0 Transport errors: 0 Server health afterward: HTTP 200 ``` This isolates the failure to the interaction involving `ngram_gpu` speculative decoding. ## Reproduction on vLLM 0.26.0 The same interaction was previously reproduced with vLLM 0.26.0. One run produced: ```text Single structured request: HTTP 200 Concurrent requests: 3 HTTP 200, 21 HTTP 500 ``` A separate run with asynchronous scheduling produced: ```text Single structured request: HTTP 200 Concurrent requests: 2 HTTP 200, 22 HTTP 500 ``` The same server-side FSM and rejected-token errors were observed. The failure therefore reproduces on both: ```text vLLM 0.26.0 vLLM 0.27.1 ``` ## Expected behavior All valid concurrent structured-output requests should complete successfully. Speculative decoding may change performance, but it should not cause xgrammar to reject tokens that have already been accepted or committed by the scheduler. Expected result: ```text 24 HTTP 200 responses 24 valid JSON outputs 0 HTTP 500 responses ``` ## Actual behavior With `ngram_gpu` enabled: ```text 3 HTTP 200 responses 21 HTTP 500 responses ``` The structured-output FSM rejects generated tokens, the affected requests are terminated, and clients receive an internal server error. ## Reproducibility summary | Configuration | Single request | Concurrent result | Server after test | |---|---:|---:|---:| | vLLM 0.27.1, xgrammar + ngram_gpu | Pass | 3/24 pass, 21 HTTP 500 | Healthy | | vLLM 0.27.1, xgrammar without speculative decoding | Pass | 24/24 pass | Healthy | | vLLM 0.26.0, xgrammar + ngram_gpu | Pass | 3/24 pass, 21 HTTP 500 | Healthy | | vLLM 0.26.0, xgrammar + ngram_gpu, separate scheduling run | Pass | 2/24 pass, 22 HTTP 500 | Healthy | ## Attached evidence [result.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143667/result.json) [ngram_gpu_stdout.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143672/ngram_gpu_stdout.log) [ngram_gpu_stderr.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143685/ngram_gpu_stderr.log) [no_spec_control_stdout.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143690/no_spec_control_stdout.log) [no_spec_control_stderr.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143699/no_spec_control_stderr.log) ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary LMCache prefill/decode disaggregation returns incorrect generation results after an apparently successful remote KV-cache transfer. The prefill and decode servers both: - Start successfully. - Return HTTP 200. - Remain healthy after the requests. - Report that LMCache P/D mode is enabled. - Report that the NIXL/UCX transfer channel is active. - Report complete prompt KV-cache hits on the decode receiver. Despite this, the P/D generation diverges from an equivalent monolithic vLLM server starting at generated token 0. The incorrect output frequently begins by reproducing tokens from inside the repeated prompt body: ```text alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta ... ``` The monolithic server instead begins answering the instruction at the end of the prompt: ```text The problem is to summarize the operational sequence ... ``` This is a silent correctness failure. It is not a startup failure, HTTP failure, missing-transfer failure, or unhealthy-engine failure. The issue was reproduced locally: - 6/6 comparisons failed across two independent vLLM 0.26.0 runs. - 3/3 comparisons failed in a separate vLLM 0.27.1 run. - Total: 9/9 LMCache P/D versus monolithic comparisons failed. - Native NIXL and Mooncake passed the identical monolithic-equivalence oracle. ## Environment Primary reproduction environment: ```text OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64) CPU: AMD EPYC 9554 64-Core Processor GPU: NVIDIA L40S Prefill: 1 × L40S Decode: 1 × independent L40S NVIDIA driver: 595.71.05 Python: 3.12.13 vLLM: 0.26.0 LMCache: 0.5.3-g140819c9 NIXL: 1.3.2 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 Transformers: 5.14.1 Model: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B Model dtype: bfloat16 KV-cache dtype: bfloat16 Tensor parallel size: 1 Execution mode: eager Transfer channel: NIXL NIXL backend: UCX ``` The same failure was independently reproduced with: ```text Python: 3.12.13 vLLM: 0.27.1 LMCache: 0.5.3-g140819c9 NIXL: 1.3.2 PyTorch: 2.13.0 Transformers: 5.15.0 Model: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B GPU: NVIDIA L40S Model dtype: bfloat16 KV-cache dtype: bfloat16 Tensor parallel size: 1 Execution mode: eager ``` ## LMCache prefill configuration Save as `lmcache_prefill.yaml`: ```yaml local_cpu: false max_local_cpu_size: 0 remote_serde: null enable_pd: true transfer_channel: "nixl" pd_role: "sender" pd_buffer_size: 1073741824 pd_buffer_device: "cuda" nixl_backends: [UCX] pd_proxy_host: "127.0.0.1" pd_proxy_port: 37413 pd_skip_proxy_notification: true ``` ## LMCache decode configuration Save as `lmcache_decode.yaml`: ```yaml local_cpu: false max_local_cpu_size: 0 remote_serde: null enable_pd: true transfer_channel: "nixl" pd_role: "receiver" pd_buffer_size: 1073741824 pd_buffer_device: "cuda" nixl_backends: [UCX] pd_peer_host: "127.0.0.1" pd_peer_init_port: [37413] pd_peer_alloc_port: [42727] ``` The exact port numbers can be replaced with any two unused local ports. The values above are taken from one representative reproduction. ## Common environment variables Run the following before starting the servers: ```bash export LMCACHE_USE_EXPERIMENTAL=True export PYTHONHASHSEED=123 export UCX_TLS=cuda_ipc,cuda_copy,tcp export VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=1 export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn export VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 ``` ## Start the prefill server ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ LMCACHE_CONFIG_FILE="$PWD/lmcache_prefill.yaml" \ python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --served-model-name veritas-model \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8100 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --max-model-len 2048 \ --max-num-seqs 8 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.65 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --disable-log-stats \ --enforce-eager \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"LMCacheConnectorV1","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"discard_partial_chunks":false,"lmcache_rpc_port":"veritas-prefill"}}' ``` Wait until `GET /v1/models` returns HTTP 200. ## Start the decode server ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \ LMCACHE_CONFIG_FILE="$PWD/lmcache_decode.yaml" \ python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --served-model-name veritas-model \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8200 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --max-model-len 2048 \ --max-num-seqs 8 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.65 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --disable-log-stats \ --enforce-eager \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"LMCacheConnectorV1","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"discard_partial_chunks":false,"lmcache_rpc_port":"veritas-decode"}}' ``` Wait until `GET /v1/models` returns HTTP 200. ## Input Three independent prompts are generated. Each prompt contains a unique random request marker to prevent accidental reuse between repetitions. ```python import uuid repeat = 0 marker = f"VERITAS_PD_{repeat}_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}" prompt = ( f"Request marker {marker}. " + "alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta " * 96 + "\nSummarize the operational sequence in exactly three short bullets." ) request_id = f"veritas-pd-{repeat}-{uuid.uuid4().hex}" ``` Depending on how the random marker is tokenized, the complete prompt contains approximately 895–898 tokens. The same exact `prompt` and `request_id` are used for the corresponding prefill and decode requests. ## Prefill request ```python import requests prefill_payload = { "model": "veritas-model", "prompt": prompt, "temperature": 0.0, "stream": False, "max_tokens": 1, "kv_transfer_params": { "disagg_spec": { "req_id": request_id, "receiver_host": "127.0.0.1", "receiver_init_port": [37413], "receiver_alloc_port": [42727], } }, } prefill_response = requests.post( "http://127.0.0.1:8100/v1/completions", json=prefill_payload, headers={"X-Request-Id": request_id}, timeout=180, ) print("prefill status:", prefill_response.status_code) print("prefill body:", prefill_response.text) ``` Observed result: ```text prefill status: 200 ``` ## Decode request After the prefill request finishes, send the same prompt and request ID to the decode receiver: ```python decode_payload = { "model": "veritas-model", "prompt": prompt, "temperature": 0.0, "seed": 0, "max_tokens": 64, "logprobs": 5, "stream": False, } decode_response = requests.post( "http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/completions", json=decode_payload, headers={"X-Request-Id": request_id}, timeout=180, ) print("decode status:", decode_response.status_code) print("decode body:", decode_response.text) ``` Observed result: ```text decode status: 200 ``` Repeat this process three times with three independently generated markers and request IDs. ## Monolithic control After recording the P/D outputs, stop both the prefill and decode servers. Start a monolithic server without LMCache or any other KV connector: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --served-model-name veritas-model \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8300 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --max-model-len 2048 \ --max-num-seqs 8 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.65 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --disable-log-stats \ --enforce-eager ``` Replay each previously recorded prompt byte-for-byte: ```python monolithic_payload = { "model": "veritas-model", "prompt": prompt, "temperature": 0.0, "seed": 0, "max_tokens": 64, "logprobs": 5, "stream": False, } monolithic_response = requests.post( "http://127.0.0.1:8300/v1/completions", json=monolithic_payload, headers={"X-Request-Id": f"mono-{request_id}"}, timeout=180, ) print("monolithic status:", monolithic_response.status_code) print("monolithic body:", monolithic_response.text) ``` Observed result: ```text monolithic status: 200 ``` ## Comparison oracle For every prompt, compare the P/D result with the monolithic result using: 1. Generated token strings. 2. Generated text. 3. Selected-token log probabilities. 4. Top-5 token overlap at each generated position. The equivalence requirements are: ```text Generated tokens must be identical. Generated text must be identical. Maximum selected-token logprob absolute difference must be <= 0.25. Minimum top-5 overlap across generated positions must be >= 0.80. ``` The following inputs are identical between the P/D decode and monolithic control: ```text Prompt bytes Model Model dtype Execution mode Temperature Seed Maximum generated tokens Requested logprob count Prefix-caching setting ``` ## LMCache transfer evidence In a representative vLLM 0.26.0 run, the LMCache decode receiver logged: ```text Reqid: cmpl-veritas-pd-0-... Total tokens 895 Inference Engine computed tokens: 0 LMCache hit tokens: 895 need to load: 894 ``` ```text Reqid: cmpl-veritas-pd-1-... Total tokens 897 Inference Engine computed tokens: 0 LMCache hit tokens: 897 need to load: 896 ``` ```text Reqid: cmpl-veritas-pd-2-... Total tokens 897 Inference Engine computed tokens: 0 LMCache hit tokens: 897 need to load: 896 ``` In the vLLM 0.27.1 confirmation run, the receiver similarly logged: ```text Reqid: cmpl-veritas-pd-0-... Total tokens 897 Inference Engine computed tokens: 0 LMCache hit tokens: 897 need to load: 896 ``` ```text Reqid: cmpl-veritas-pd-1-... Total tokens 897 Inference Engine computed tokens: 0 LMCache hit tokens: 897 need to load: 896 ``` ```text Reqid: cmpl-veritas-pd-2-... Total tokens 895 Inference Engine computed tokens: 0 LMCache hit tokens: 895 need to load: 894 ``` The connector evidence collected from the server logs was: ```json { "lmcache_initialized": true, "pd_enabled": true, "nixl_channel": true, "cache_retrieval": true, "healthy_engine": true } ``` ## Representative output mismatch For one vLLM 0.26.0 repetition, the LMCache P/D output began with: ```text alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta ``` Its first generated tokens were: ```json [ " alpha", " beta", " gamma", " delta", " epsilon", " z", "eta", " eta", " theta", " alpha", " beta", " gamma" ] ``` For the identical prompt, the monolithic output began with: ```text The problem is to summarize the operational sequence in exactly three short bullets. ``` Its first generated tokens were: ```json [ " \n\n", "The", " problem", " is", " to", " summarize", " the", " operational", " sequence", " in", " exactly", " three" ] ``` The P/D and monolithic generations therefore diverged at generated token 0. A second prompt produced the following P/D output: ```text alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. ``` The monolithic server instead produced: ```text The first step is to identify the key elements of the system. The second step is to determine the appropriate tools and methods to achieve the goal. The third step is to implement the solution. ``` ## vLLM 0.26.0 results ### Independent run 1 ```text Prompt 0: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.4423 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 Prompt 1: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.6104 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 Prompt 2: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.3309 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 ``` ### Independent run 2 ```text Prompt 0: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.3705 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 Prompt 1: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.4516 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 Prompt 2: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.3782 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 ``` Result: ```text 6/6 LMCache P/D comparisons failed. All six comparisons diverged at generated token 0. ``` ## vLLM 0.27.1 results ```text Prompt 0: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.6067 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 Prompt 1: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.6052 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 Prompt 2: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 2.5831 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 ``` Result: ```text 3/3 LMCache P/D comparisons failed. All three comparisons diverged at generated token 0. ``` ## Native NIXL control The identical three prompts and monolithic-equivalence oracle were run using the native vLLM NIXL connector. ```text Prompt 0: tokens_equal: true text_equal: true maximum selected-token logprob difference: 0.0479 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.8 Prompt 1: tokens_equal: true text_equal: true maximum selected-token logprob difference: 0.0893 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.8 Prompt 2: tokens_equal: true text_equal: true maximum selected-token logprob difference: 0.0621 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.8 ``` Native NIXL verdict: ```text pass ``` ## Mooncake control The identical three prompts and monolithic-equivalence oracle were also run using the Mooncake connector. ```text Prompt 0: tokens_equal: true text_equal: true maximum selected-token logprob difference: 0.0942 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.8 Prompt 1: tokens_equal: true text_equal: true maximum selected-token logprob difference: 0.1162 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.8 Prompt 2: tokens_equal: true text_equal: true maximum selected-token logprob difference: 0.0640 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.8 ``` Mooncake verdict: ```text pass ``` These controls use the same: ```text Model Prompt generation Prompt lengths GPU type BF16 dtype Temperature Seed Maximum generated token count Logprob count Monolithic-equivalence oracle ``` ## Reproducibility summary | Runtime | Connector | Comparisons | Result | |---|---|---:|---| | vLLM 0.26.0 / LMCache 0.5.3-g140819c9, run 1 | LMCache | 3 | 3 mismatches | | vLLM 0.26.0 / LMCache 0.5.3-g140819c9, run 2 | LMCache | 3 | 3 mismatches | | vLLM 0.27.1 / LMCache 0.5.3-g140819c9 | LMCache | 3 | 3 mismatches | | vLLM 0.26.0 | Native NIXL | 3 | 3 equivalent | | vLLM 0.26.0 | Mooncake | 3 | 3 equivalent | Overall LMCache result: ```text 9/9 P/D versus monolithic comparisons mismatched. ``` ## Expected behavior When the LMCache receiver reports that the complete prompt KV cache was retrieved, decoding should be semantically equivalent to running the same prompt on a monolithic server with the same model and sampling configuration. In particular: - The first generated token should match. - The complete generated token sequence should match. - The generated text should match. - Token log probabilities should remain within normal BF16 numerical tolerance. - Top-k distributions should retain substantial overlap. ## Actual behavior The LMCache receiver reports a complete KV-cache hit and returns HTTP 200, but: - The first generated token differs from the monolithic result. - The complete 64-token output differs. - Generated text differs. - Minimum top-5 overlap reaches 0.0. - Maximum selected-token logprob differences reach approximately 2.58–3.61. - Output frequently begins with tokens taken from inside the repeated prompt body. - Both servers remain healthy. - No explicit runtime error is returned to the client. ## Classification This appears to be a remote KV restoration correctness failure rather than a transfer availability failure. The evidence shows that: - LMCache initializes successfully. - P/D mode is enabled. - The NIXL/UCX transfer path is active. - The receiver reports complete cache hits. - The inference engine reports zero computed prompt tokens. - Prefill and decode requests both return HTTP 200. - Both engines remain healthy. - The restored KV state does not preserve the expected next-token semantics. ## Reproduce * The full reproduction script can be seen here [repro_lmcache_pd.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31142926/repro_lmcache_pd.py). * Run it with 2 separate GPUs. `.../miniconda3/envs/vllm_0260/bin/python repro_lmcache_pd.py --prefill-gpu 0 --decode-gpu 1 --out-dir artifacts` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Doc]: vLLM's default NIXL connector is ~100× slower than the push connector on non-RDMA hardware, and the fix is undocumented
items.body:
### 📚 The doc issue

[cuda_ipc_probe.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31139915/cuda_ipc_probe.py)
[nixl_bench.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31139914/nixl_bench.py)
[nixl-bench-pods.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31139913/nixl-bench-pods.yaml)

## Summary

On hardware without RDMA, where prefill and decode share a node, vLLM's
`NixlConnector` transfers KV cache at **0.5 GB/s**. Switching a single config
value to `NixlPushConnector` gives **49 GB/s** on the same hardware, same pods,
same NIXL and UCX build — a **~100× difference** that matches raw CUDA peer-copy
bandwidth.

Cause: **NIXL/UCX `cuda_ipc` serves remote PUT at full speed but falls back to
TCP for remote GET.** vLLM's `pull_worker.py` issues `make_prepped_xfer("READ", ...)`,
and `NixlConnector` is a backward-compatible **alias for `NixlPullConnector`**,
so the familiar connector name silently selects the slow direction.

This is defensible design for the hardware NIXL targets: on InfiniBand or RoCE,
RDMA READ and RDMA WRITE are symmetric at line rate, so a pull-based connector
costs nothing and arguably reads better, since the consumer controls when it
fetches. The asymmetry only appears on `cuda_ipc`, which is only reachable for
same-node transfers without RDMA. Anyone deploying on an RDMA fabric would never
see this.

The problem is discoverability. `NixlPushConnector` does not appear in vLLM's
NixlConnector documentation, and a web search for the name returns no results.
A user on commodity GPU nodes therefore hits a 100× regression with no
indication that a supported fix exists.

---

## Environment

| item | value |
|---|---|
| Host | Google Cloud `g4-standard-96` (also reproduced on `g4-standard-384`) |
| GPUs | 2 × NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), 96 GB |
| Interconnect | **PCIe P2P, no NVLink, no RDMA.** `nvidia-smi topo -m` = `PIX`, `can_device_access_peer(0,1) = True` |
| Driver | 580 |
| Image | `docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1` |
| NIXL | vendored 1.3.1/1.3.2; **also reproduced with 1.4.0** installed via pip |
| Orchestration | reproduced both on GKE and on a bare VM with Docker |

---

## Measurements

### 1. The asymmetry, isolated from vLLM

`bench/nixl_bench.py` calls `nixl._api` directly — no vLLM, no model, no KV
cache. Two processes, one GPU each, 2.15 GB per transfer:

| op | API | descriptors | Gbit/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| WRITE | `initialize_xfer` | 1 | 383.92 |
| WRITE | `initialize_xfer` | 614 | 370.67 |
| WRITE | `make_prepped_xfer` | 1 | 413.99 |
| WRITE | `make_prepped_xfer` | 614 | 414.33 |
| **READ** | `initialize_xfer` | 1 | **3.91** |
| **READ** | `initialize_xfer` | 614 | **4.19** |
| **READ** | `make_prepped_xfer` | 1 | **4.20** |
| **READ** | `make_prepped_xfer` | 614 | **4.21** |

The operation is the only variable that matters. The prepped-descriptor API
versus `initialize_xfer` makes no difference, and descriptor count makes none
either, so this is not batching or launch overhead.

### 2. The same asymmetry through vLLM

Identical pods, identical settings, only `kv_connector` changed. Single request
with a 30,067-token prompt, measured from `vllm:nixl_bytes_transferred_sum` and
`vllm:nixl_xfer_time_seconds_sum`:

| `kv_connector` | bytes | time | bandwidth |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NixlConnector` (= `NixlPullConnector`, READ) | 2158 MB | 4.354 s | **0.50 GB/s** |
| `NixlPushConnector` (WRITE) | 2158 MB | 0.044 s | **49.04 GB/s** |

49 GB/s matches raw CUDA peer copy on this host (48–51 GB/s), so the push path
reaches full hardware bandwidth.

### 3. Reference bandwidths on the same host

| path | bandwidth |
|---|---|
| Raw CUDA peer copy GPU0→GPU1 | 48–51 GB/s |
| Raw CUDA IPC peer copy, two processes | 55.4 GB/s |
| `iperf3` TCP loopback, single stream | 12 GB/s |
| `iperf3` pod-to-pod, same node | 8.2 GB/s |
| `iperf3` pod-to-pod, **cross-node** | 4.7 GB/s (37.5 Gbit/s); 21.6 GB/s with 8 streams |
| NIXL READ path | 0.5 GB/s |

Note the READ path is slower than plain TCP loopback by 24×, so it is not simply
"falling back to the network"; it is well under what the network itself
delivers.

---

## What was ruled out

Each tested individually, with a redeploy and measurement:

1. **Kubernetes.** Reproduced on a bare VM with Docker and no CNI.
2. **Network bandwidth and latency.** 65.5 Gbit/s pod-to-pod, 0.016 ms RTT.
3. **Descriptor batching.** Flat from 1 to 2048 descriptors.
4. **NIXL version.** 1.4.0 behaves identically to 1.3.x.
5. **`--enable-cumem-allocator`.** vLLM's NixlConnector guide states the KV cache
   must be registered as VMM via this flag or NIXL "can only use RDMA/TCP".
   Removing it changed nothing measurable here. Worth reviewing: CUDA VMM
   allocations are not exportable via `cudaIpcGetMemHandle`, so the guidance may
   be counterproductive for the CUDA IPC path it describes.
6. **`UCX_CUDA_IPC_ENABLE_MNNVL=y`**, also from that guide. On non-MNNVL hardware
   it logs `cuda_ipc_md.c:562 UCX ERROR multi-node NVLINK support is requested
   but not supported`. Removing it did not restore bandwidth, but the error
   suggests the flag should be conditional on MNNVL hardware.
7. **`UCX_TLS` list and `UCX_MEMTYPE_CACHE`.** No material effect.
8. **Privileges.** Both processes run as root with `CAP_IPC_LOCK`.

---

## Deployment preconditions found along the way

These are not the bug, but they are undocumented and each silently costs the
fast path. On GKE all of the following were required before `cuda_ipc` could be
selected between pods at all:

| setting | symptom when missing |
|---|---|
| `privileged: true` | The NVIDIA device plugin restricts GPUs through the cgroup device controller. `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all` alone still leaves `nvidia-smi -L` showing one GPU even though `/dev/nvidia0..7` are mounted. |
| `hostPID: true` | `cudaIpcOpenMemHandle` returns `invalid device context (201)` |
| `hostIPC: true` | necessary, not sufficient alone |
| peer GPU visible to the importing container | `cudaIpcOpenMemHandle` returns `invalid argument (1)` |

`hostNetwork` is **not** required; it also collides on ports, since both llm-d
roles bind 8000 and 5600.

Note the security cost: privileged plus host PID/IPC makes Kubernetes GPU
isolation advisory. That trade-off deserves to be stated in any guide that
recommends same-node disaggregation.

---

## Suggested asks

1. **Document `NixlPushConnector`.** It currently appears nowhere in the
   NixlConnector usage guide and is not web-searchable.
2. **State the direction trade-off.** Recommend push on non-RDMA hardware and
   explain that pull is intended for fabrics where READ and WRITE are symmetric.
3. **Warn at runtime.** When a NIXL agent connects to a co-located peer and the
   selected transport for the transfer direction is not `cuda_ipc`, log a
   warning naming the transport. Today the degradation is silent and only
   discoverable by measuring.
4. **Revisit `--enable-cumem-allocator` and `UCX_CUDA_IPC_ENABLE_MNNVL`
   guidance**, which appear to be written for MNNVL systems and are at best
   inert, at worst counterproductive, elsewhere.
5. **Upstream to `ai-dynamo/nixl`:** is the PUT/GET asymmetry on `cuda_ipc`
   expected, or is remote GET simply not implemented for that transport? If
   expected, NIXL could surface it so callers can choose direction accordingly.

---

## Reproducers

- `nixl_bench.py` — NIXL transfer benchmark, sweeps READ/WRITE ×
  simple/prepped × descriptor count. No vLLM, no model.
- `cuda_ipc_probe.py` — raw `cudaIpcGetMemHandle`/`cudaIpcOpenMemHandle`
  across an arbitrary boundary, with a same-container control.
- `nixl-bench-pods.yaml` — runs the benchmark as two GKE pods.

Two implementation notes for anyone adapting these. The CUDA IPC handle must be
carried as `c_ubyte[64]`; `c_char[64]` truncates it at the first NUL and yields
a false negative. And the metadata-exchange directory must be wiped between
runs, or the target sees a stale done-flag, exits immediately, and the initiator
fails with `NIXL_ERR_BACKEND` against dead agent metadata.

---

## Related upstream material

- [vllm-project/vllm#26382](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/26382) —
  NIXL slowness on CUDA_IPC, attributed to transmission time and fixed with
  patched builds adding batching. Our descriptor sweep shows batching is not the
  mechanism; direction is.
- [ai-dynamo/nixl#791](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/issues/791) — low
  saturated bandwidth via the UCX backend.
- [ai-dynamo/nixl#1614](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/issues/1614) —
  `NIXL_ERR_BACKEND` cross-node, `UCX_CUDA_IPC_ENABLE_MNNVL` discussion.
- [NVIDIA Dynamo disaggregated communication guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/dynamo/kubernetes-deployment/operate/disagg-communication)
  — describes `cuda_ipc` as "same-node, same-pod" and notes NVLink P2P needs a
  single process. Dynamo also uses NIXL, so the same asymmetry should be
  expected there on non-RDMA hardware.
- [vLLM NixlConnector usage guide](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/features/nixl_connector_usage/)
  — the page that should mention `NixlPushConnector` and does not.

---

AI assistance was used in this project.

items.title: [Bug]: GPT-OSS reasoning retains matched stop string when include_stop_str_in_output=false
items.body:
### Your current environment

```text
vLLM version: 0.27.0
Model: openai/gpt-oss-20b
Precision: MXFP4
TP/PP: 1/1
Endpoint: /v1/chat/completions
Streaming: false
```

This was observed in a downstream deployment based on vLLM v0.27.0. I have not yet reproduced it with the official upstream container.

### Describe the bug

For a non-streaming GPT-OSS chat completion, vLLM detects a stop string in the reasoning output but returns that same stop string even when `include_stop_str_in_output` is `false`.

Request:

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "openai/gpt-oss-20b",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "Can you write me a song?"}
    ],
    "temperature": 0,
    "max_tokens": 500,
    "min_tokens": 0,
    "stop": ["song", "verse", "chorus", "bridge", "stanza", "melody"],
    "include_stop_str_in_output": false
  }'
```

The response had `content=null`, `finish_reason="stop"`, and `stop_reason="song"`. The returned `reasoning` text still ended with `song`, so the matched stop string remained in the response.

### Expected behavior

With `include_stop_str_in_output=false`, the matched stop string should not be present in returned output. In this case, reasoning should end before `song`, or the API contract should explicitly document that reasoning is exempt from stop-string removal.

The current `SamplingParams.stop` documentation says that returned output will not contain stop strings. `include_stop_str_in_output` is also documented as controlling whether stop strings are included in output text.

### Why this matters

Reasoning models can stop before producing final content, leaving `content=null`. A client cannot validate stop-string exclusion by checking only `content`; the only returned model text is in `reasoning`.

This also makes it unclear whether the problem is in engine stop-string truncation or in the GPT-OSS reasoning parser after the generated text is split into reasoning and content.

### Related issues

- #51641 covers a streaming Qwen3 stop-buffer desynchronization. This report is non-streaming and uses the GPT-OSS reasoning parser.
- #38789 reported another streaming reasoning-parser interaction with stop sequences.

- [x] I searched open and closed issues for `include_stop_str_in_output`, GPT-OSS, stop strings, and reasoning parser behavior.

### 🐛 Describe the bug **Build note.** I am on the commit-pinned muse_glimmer image (`vllm/vllm-openai:v99a10304dce8945119bd0b1a072297803c52a749-ubuntu2404`, reported by `collect_env.py` as `0.26.1rc1.dev608+g99a10304d`). The published v0.27.0 and v0.27.1 releases do not include Muse Glimmer support, so I cannot retest on a tagged release yet. #51655 merged two days ago, and `vllm/reasoning/muse_glimmer_reasoning_parser.py` in this image is byte-identical to the file now on `main`, so what follows is not an artefact of the pre-merge build. **With `--reasoning-parser muse_glimmer`, asking for a JSON schema forces a trade-off: depending on `structured_outputs.enable_in_reasoning`, you can have reasoning or an enforced schema, but never both.** | `enable_in_reasoning` | `message.reasoning` | JSON schema | |---|---|---| | `True` | ❌ empty — the grammar masks from token 0, so the model never gets to open a `to=self` channel | ✅ enforced | | `False` (default) | ✅ correct | ❌ **silently not enforced** | With `enable_in_reasoning=False` the request returns 200, but nothing comes back in the requested JSON schema. ### Why it happens `MuseGlimmerReasoningParser` reports a reasoning end only when a **tool** channel opens. The decode-time predicate delegates straight to the tool-only one (`vllm/reasoning/muse_glimmer_reasoning_parser.py`, current `main`): ````python def is_reasoning_end_streaming( self, input_ids: Sequence[int], delta_ids: Iterable[int] ) -> bool: return self.is_reasoning_end(list(input_ids)) ```` and its docstring states the tool-only rule is deliberate: > A `to=user` answer is NOT a reason to leave the reasoning phase -- this parser > surfaces that content itself. Only a real tool channel switches the > `DelegatingParser` phase machine over to the tool parser. **That looks reasonable.** Muse Glimmer runs with `skip_special_tokens=False`, so framing markers survive into the decoded text. When no schema is involved the parser splits the `to=self` and `to=user` bodies itself and emits them clean. If it reported a reasoning end at `to=user`, the serving phase machine would hand a plain prose answer to the ATEM tool parser, which would see a bare `<|message|>`, misclassify it as the content channel, and leak framing into content. That said, `to=user` is where the model starts answering the user. Other reasoning parsers treat exactly that boundary as the end of reasoning: for a ``-style model, everything after `` is the user-facing answer, and that is where the grammar is allowed to start. Muse Glimmer's `to=user` channel is the same boundary expressed in a different framing, so it is reasonable to expect structured outputs to behave the same way here. With the current code base, however, structured outputs cannot follow that same boundary. A **second** consumer reads the same predicate to answer a **different** question: | Consumer | Question it asks | |---|---| | `DelegatingParser.parse_delta` | When should the stream go to the tool parser? | | `vllm/v1/structured_output/` | When may the grammar bitmask start being filled? | For a ``-style parser both questions share one answer, so the overload is invisible. Muse Glimmer has a separate answer channel and tool channel, and the two consumers want different answers at the same moment — which is why no single return value satisfies both, and why better detection alone cannot fix it. On a plain answer turn no tool channel is ever opened, so `reasoning_ended` never becomes `True`, `should_fill_bitmask()` keeps returning `False`, and the bitmask is never filled. The schema is never applied. ### Reproduce ````bash # stock image, no parser modifications vllm serve \ --reasoning-parser muse_glimmer \ --tool-call-parser muse_glimmer \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"reasoning_strength":"low"}' # structured_outputs.enable_in_reasoning is left at its default (False) ```` ````bash curl localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "model": "", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Summarise this in the given schema."}], "response_format": {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": { "name": "s", "schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"scenario": {"type": "string"}, "confidence": {"type": "number"}}, "required": ["scenario", "confidence"], "additionalProperties": false}}}, "max_tokens": 8192 }' ```` The schema is requested per-request through `response_format` on the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, not through a server-side flag — so vLLM does receive a well-formed schema request on the supported path. - **Observed:** the schema is not enforced. `message.content` comes back as free-form prose bearing no relation to the schema, with no error and no warning — every downstream node that parses these responses fell through to its deterministic fallback. `message.reasoning` is populated correctly. - **Expected:** `message.content` validates against the schema, and `message.reasoning` carries the `to=self` channel. Channel splitting itself is fine — `extract_reasoning` separates the bodies correctly. The only thing that fails is grammar activation. ### Proposed change Report the reasoning end at the `to=user` header, but **only in `is_reasoning_end_streaming()`** — the predicate the engine consults during decoding. The grammar then starts on the first token of the answer body, leaving the `to=self` channel unconstrained. Leave `is_reasoning_end()` tool-only. Every caller of that overload evaluates it against **prompt** token-ids, where a generated `to=user` header cannot appear, so widening it buys no decode-time behaviour; and since `_current_assistant_turn()` falls back to the whole text when there is no `<|start|>assistant`, an assistant-prefill or `continue_final_message` request would enter the tool phase at token 0. We have been running this patched parser in production, and both fields come back correctly: unconstrained reasoning in `message.reasoning`, and a schema-conformant object in `message.content`. **Existing behaviour is preserved.** We ran the patched parser against the current one on the same inputs: `_classify_bodies` and `extract_reasoning` produce byte-identical output, and the tool-handoff path is untouched. This adds a capability rather than trading one off. One complication remains: the serving phase machine calls the same streaming predicate and must **not** flip at `to=user`. In our deployment we gate the new branch on the instance never having been used as a streaming extractor — `parse_delta` calls `extract_reasoning_streaming()` before `is_reasoning_end_streaming()`, while the structured-output gate never calls the extractors at all. It works, but it couples the parser to an undocumented call ordering, so I would not propose shipping it as-is. Cleaner directions, in rough order of preference: 1. A separate predicate for the structured-output gate (e.g. `is_grammar_start_allowed()`) whose default delegates to the existing one, so no current parser changes behaviour. 2. Pass the consuming role to the reasoning parser at construction time. 3. At minimum, log a warning when a structured-output request finishes with the bitmask never having been filled, so this stops being a silent failure. Related: #39130 was the same symptom on `gemma4` with a different cause — there the end marker was absent from the prompt, and #45553 / #45588 fixed it by pre-initialising the parser engine from prompt state. Gemma 4 has a single boundary (everything after the channel close is content), so one predicate suffices there. I have a patch and unit tests for the parser-local version, and am happy to open a PR in whichever direction maintainers prefer. cc @xianbaoqian @jeejeelee ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
